text: {"score":3,"justification":"Core numbers match the card (13.7%, 3.1%, 5.44, z 1.70, 45 docs, 20 99215 docs, 0 below, 33/1). The leaning and cautious tone are reasonable. However, several claims are unsupported or wrong: the \"every sampled 99215 chart supports the billed level\" headline is overstated, the \"share is elevated in every stratum 0 to 4\" claim is partly misleading, and note-sign figures (problems 16%, late 9%, repeated-time signals) are not on the card. Citations fit imperfectly, and the next steps are generic and partly mismatched to the cited claims.","problems":["The \"16%\" problems share cannot be matched to the card, and the late 9%, unsigned 0%, data 2% and audit-trail statements are not on the card. They may come from tool output, but they are not verifiable here.","Claims C0201534 is \"among the notes flagged for problems\" and has \"repeated-time signals\"; the card shows only that it is documented high MDM with 48 minutes, so the flag is unsupported.","Headline says \"every sampled 99215 chart supports the billed level\", but only 20 of 71 99215 claims were documented. Describing that as \"every sampled\" is overstated.","Cited claims C0201456 and C0201454 are described as \"simple acute diagnoses such as URI, UTI and rash\"; C0201454 and C0201456 are UTI (N39.0), and the card shows no documentation for them, so the citation adds little. The 23% figure rounds the card's 22.5%.","The claim that share is elevated in every stratum 0-4 is fine, but the 5+ stratum is not mentioned (it is lower than the all-provider share); this is minor.","Next steps are generic and the example claims are code-formatted; the one documented below-billed claim (C0201909) is listed first, but its relevance to a targeted 99215 sample is unclear.","The rationale is long and repetitive, and hedges both ways, leaving the investigator to decide."]}
